newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Poland wants more EU aid to meet veterinary standards.
newsitem.headline: Poland wants more EU aid to meet veterinary standards.

text.p: Polish Deputy Prime Minister Roman Jaglelinski said on Wednesday he wanted more European Union aid to help match EU veterinary and plant health standards.
Speaking through an interpreter, Jaglelinski told journalists after meeting EU farm ministers that his dream would be 1.2 billion ecus in the agriculture sector.
"We already get 12 million from the EU's PHARE aid programme but we need ten times that just for agriculture," he said.
He added that the figure was an unlikely target and he confirmed that political changes in the ruling alliance of Polish parties would not affect his country's pro-Europe stance.
"We have the laws and a Prime Minister who will ensure that Poland remains positive about membership of the European Union," he said.

Earlier he told farm ministers meeting government leaders from east European and Baltic applicant countries that with the eastern border of Poland due to become the EU frontier after proposed enlargement that there was an urgent need for specialist veterinary equipment.
He told the meeting: "Immediate improvement of the border check-point infrastructure is required to cope with this challenge."
He described as "expensive" veterinary laboratory equipment and the cost of developing animal identification and registration systems in line with those discussed in the EU.

Failure to meet hopes raised by the announcement of pre- accession funding is now being compounded by the inability to implement measures caused by a deterioration of the agri-food sector in Poland, he said.
After the meeting an EU member state official said that farm Commissioner Franz Fischler had stressed the importance of keeping animal diseases out of an enlarged EU.

"Not surprisingly the emphasis placed on keeping animal and plant diseases from getting into neighbouring applicant countries was a factor in a number of them stressing that they could use more financial assistance in this respect," the official said.
